Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:12:1.hebrew: התם היינו טעמא - דשניהם נשבעין ונוטלין, דחנוני אומר לבעל הבית: אנא שליחותא דידך עבדי, ונתתי לפועלך ממון שצויתני:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:12:1.english: There, this is the reason - That both of them take an oath and collect [is] because the storekeeper says to the homeowner: "I carried out your agency, and I gave your laborer the money you instructed me [to give]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:12:2.english: What do I have [to do] with the hired laborer - To dispute [with him].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:12:3.hebrew: לא מהימן לי - איני מאמינו בשבועה. אני אומר שהוא רשע, ואין לי להאמין אדם בשבועה על כרחי, אלא אם כן האמנתיו מתחילה להפקיד אצלו או להתנות עמו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:12:3.english: He is not trustworthy to me - I do not believe him under oath. I say that he is wicked, and I am not obligated to believe a person under oath against my will, unless I trusted him from the outset to deposit [property] with him or to make stipulations with him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:12:4.hebrew: את הימנתיה - ואתה הוא שקילקלת, ואין לי להפסיד בקלקולך, שיהיו מעותי מונחין עד שיבא אליהו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:12:4.english: You trusted him - And you are the one who caused the problem, and I should not suffer a loss through your fault, such that my money should be set aside until Elijah comes.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:14:1.hebrew: וישבע על השאר - כדין מודה מקצת הטענה, שאמרה תורה ישבע, כדילפינן בשבועות (דף לט:) מכי הוא זה. ואע"ג דזה לא הודה, הרי יש עדים במקצת, ולא תהא הודאת פיו גדולה לחייבו על השאר שבועה מהעדאת עדים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:14:1.english: And he shall take an oath regarding the remainder - In accordance with the law of one who admits to part of a claim, of whom the Torah stated [that] he shall take an oath, as we derive in Shevuot (39b) from "that this is it." And even though this [defendant] did not admit [to anything], behold, there are witnesses to part [of the claim], and his own admission should not be greater to obligate him in an oath on the remainder than the testimony of witnesses.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:15:1.english: From an a fortiori [inference] - Below, [the Gemara] explains what the a fortiori [inference] is.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:16:1.english: And the Tanna taught in support - And our Tanna [is] support for me [Rabbi Chiyya].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:16:2.english: This one says, etc. - And [the mishna] teaches that both of them take an oath.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:16:3.english: We are witnesses that what this one is holding - That is half.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:16:4.hebrew: דידיה הוא - שהרי מוחזק הוא בפנינו, והרי הוא תובע את כולה, וחבירו כופר את כולה, שאומר כולה שלי, ואף מה שאתה תפוס בידך, ואנו מעידין אותו שיש לו בה מקצת, ומחייבים את חבירו שבועה על השאר, דהיינו חצי שעיכב לעצמו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:16:4.english: It is his - For he is in possession [of it] before us, and he claims all of it, and his fellow denies all of it, saying: "All of it is mine, and even what you are holding in your hand." And we testify concerning him that he has a portion in it, and we obligate his fellow [to take] an oath regarding the remainder, namely, the half that he withheld for himself.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:17:1.hebrew: מאי לא תהא הודאת פיו גדולה מהעדאת עדים - מהיכי תיתי לן למידק דתיסק אדעתין דתהא הודאת פיו גדולה מהעדאת עדים, דאיצטריך לתנא למילף מק"ו דלא תהא הודאת פיו גדולה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:17:1.english: What is [the meaning of] "the admission of his own mouth should not be greater than the testimony of witnesses" - From where would we deduce [such] that it would enter our mind that the admission of his own mouth should be greater than the testimony of witnesses, such that it was necessary for the Tanna to derive from an a fortiori argument that the admission of his own mouth should not be greater?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:18:1.hebrew: מפני מה אמרה תורה כו' - ולא חשבו כמשיב אבידה לפטרו, שלא כפר בכולו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:18:1.english: Why did the Torah say, etc. - And [why] did it not consider him like one who returns a lost object, to exempt him, since he did not deny all of it?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:1:1.hebrew: ואיכא למימר כוליה דמר - ועוד, על כרחך או כוליה דמר או כוליה דמר, אפילו הכי חולקין בלא שבועה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:1:1.english: And there is room to say [that] it belongs entirely to [one] Master - And furthermore, perforce [it belongs] either entirely to [one] Master or entirely to [the other] Master, [and] even so, they divide [it] without an oath.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:1:2.english: Here, where there is no monetary loss - And furthermore, since there is room to say that both of them lifted it together.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:1:3.english: Is it not all the more so - That they divide [it] without an oath.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:3:1.hebrew: דר' יוסי - לקמן בהמפקיד (בבא מציעא דף לז.): שנים שהפקידו אצל אחד, זה מנה וזה מאתים, זה אומר מאתים שלי, וזה אומר מאתים שלי. וקאמר ת"ק: נותן לזה מנה ולזה מנה, והשאר יהא מונח עד שיבא אליהו. אמר ר' יוסי: א"כ, מה הפסיד הרמאי, ולמה יודה? הרי קיבל את שלו! אלא הכל יהא מונח, ויפסיד הרמאי. וה"נ יהא מונח:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:3:1.english: [That] of Rabbi Yosei - Below, in [the chapter] HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 37a): [In the case of] two who deposited with one [person], this one a maneh [one hundred dinars] and that one two hundred, this one says, "Two hundred are mine," and that one says, "Two hundred are mine." And the First Tanna says: He gives this one a maneh and that one a maneh, and the remainder shall be left until Elijah comes. Rabbi Yosei said: If so, what did the swindler lose, and why should he admit [the truth]? Behold, he received his own! Rather, the entire [amount] shall be left, and the swindler will lose. And here too, [the garment] should be left [lying].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:4:1.hebrew: הא נמי כשאר דמיא - דהתם על מנה השני הם דנין, ואלו דנין על הטלית כולה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:4:1.english: This too is comparable to the remainder - For there, they are litigating over the second *maneh* [one hundred dinars], while these are litigating over the entire garment.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:5:1.english: That it belongs to one of them - And one cannot say that they should divide [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:6:1.english: Here, where there is room to say that it belongs to one of them - And his fellow has no share in it, is it not all the more so that he does not hold [that] they divide [it]?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:8:1.english: What loss does he incur - To the one who has no share in it, if it is placed in storage.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:8:2.hebrew: דלודי - שאין לו חלק בה, כשיודה, מה יטול:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:8:2.english: That he will admit - Since he has no share in it, when he admits, what will he take?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:9:1.hebrew: מקח וממכר מאי איכא למימר - הא אוקימנא דקיבל דמים מתרוייהו, ואי הוה אמרינן יהא הטלית והדמים מונחים, אית ליה פסידא לרמאי, ויודה על האמת קודם שיפסיד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 3a:9:1.english: [Regarding] buying and selling, what is there to say - Behold, we established that [the seller] received payment from both of them, and if we were to say, "Let the garment and the money be deposited," the swindler would incur a loss, and he would admit the truth before he loses [his money].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:10:1.hebrew: גבי חנוני נמי יהא מונח - לר"ע, דאמר (יבמות דף קיח:) בלקח מחמשה ואינו יודע מאיזה מהם לקח, נותן לכאו"א — לא פריך: אמאי נותן לכאו"א, יהא מונח? דהתם הוה ליה למדכר, ואיהו דאפסיד אנפשיה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:10:1.english: In the case of a storekeeper too, let it be deposited - According to Rabbi Akiva, who said (Yevamot 118b) [that if one] purchased from five [people] and does not know from which of them he purchased, he gives to each and every one — [the Gemara] does not ask: "Why does he give to each and every one? Let it be deposited!" For there, he should have remembered, and he brought the loss upon himself.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:12:1.hebrew: ולא אמרת לי הב ליה בסהדי - תימה: לימא ליה בעל הבית: לתקוני שדרתיך ולא לעוותי! אע"ג דלא אמר ליה הב ליה בסהדי, היה לו מעצמו להשים על לב! כדאמרינן בפ' הכותב (כתובות דף פה.) גבי אבימי, דהוי מסקי ביה זוזי בי חוזאי, ושדרינהו ביד (רבא), ופרענהו, ואמר להו: הב לי שטרא, ואמרו ליה: הנך סטראי נינהו. ומסיק התם: דלא שנא א"ל שקול שטרא והב להו זוזי, ולא שנא הב זוזי ושקול שטרא - מחייב השליח, משום דאמר ליה: לתקוני שדרתיך ולא לעוותי. וי"ל: דהתם, כיון דהזכיר לקיחת השטר, כאילו אומר עשה באותו ענין שיבא השטר לידך; אבל הכא, לא הזכיר עדים כלל:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:12:1.english: And you did not say to me: "Give to him before witnesses" - It is puzzling: Let the employer say to him: "I sent you to benefit [me] and not to cause [me] a loss!" Even though he did not say to him: "Give to him before witnesses," he should have realized on his own, as we say in chapter HaKotev (Ketubot 85a) regarding Avimi, who owed money to people in Bei Choza'ei, and he sent it via (Rava), and he paid them, and said to them: "Give me the promissory note," and they said to him: "Those [funds] were for another debt." And [the Gemara] concludes there that it makes no difference whether he said to him: "Take the promissory note and give them the money," or: "Give the money and take the promissory note" — the agent is liable, because he says to him: "I sent you to benefit [me] and not to cause [me] a loss." And one can say that there, since he mentioned taking the promissory note, it is as if he is saying: "Act in such a manner that the promissory note will come into your possession." But here, he did not mention witnesses at all.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:18:1.hebrew: מפני מה אמרה תורה כו' - פי': יהא נאמן במגו דאי בעי כופר הכל, או נילף מהכא דלא נימא מגו בעלמא? ומשני: דאין זה מגו, דאין אדם מעיז פניו לכפור הכל, הואיל וחבירו מכיר בשקרו. אבל במקום שיכול להעיז, כגון בבנו, ואמר מנה לאביך בידי והאכלתיו פרס, נאמן במגו דאי בעי כפר הכל, כדאיתא פ"ב דכתובות (דף יח. ושם) ובפרק שבועת הדיינים (שבועות דף מב.). וא"ת: כופר הכל מנלן דפטור? ואין לומר מטעם חזקה דאין אדם מעיז, דהא אפי' במקום שיכול להעיז פטור, כגון בבנו; ואפילו מודה מקצת פטור התם, מגו דאי בעי כפר הכל. ואין לומר דילפינן מדאיצטריך למכתב שעד אחד מחייבו שבועה, ואי כופר הכל חייב מאי נפקא מינה מעד אחד, הא בלאו הכי חייב; דהא איצטריך במקום שהוא אינו תובע כלום ואינו יודע, והעד מעיד שהוא גנב או שאביו הלוה לו. וי"ל, דמכי הוא זה משמע דגזירת הכתוב הוא, דדוקא מודה מקצת הטענה חייב, ולא כופר הכל:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:18:1.english: Why did the Torah say, etc. - Meaning: [Why should he have to swear? Rather,] let him be believed by virtue of a *miggo*, for had he wanted, he could have denied everything; or [if he is not believed], shall we derive from here that we do not apply *miggo* in general? And [the Gemara] answers that this is not a [valid] *miggo*, because a person does not have the audacity to deny everything, since his fellow recognizes his lie. However, in a case where he is able to be audacious, such as [when facing the creditor's] son, and he said: "A *maneh* belonging to your father was in my possession, but I gave him half a *maneh* [a *peras*] to eat," he is believed by virtue of a *miggo* that had he wanted, he could have denied everything, as it is stated in the second chapter of Ketubot (18a and there) and in the chapter "Shevuat HaDayanim" (Shevuot 42a). And if you say: From where do we know that one who denies everything is exempt [from an oath]? And one cannot say [that it is] due to the presumption that a person is not audacious — for even in a case where he is able to be audacious he is exempt, such as [when facing] his son; and even one who admits to part is exempt there, by virtue of a *miggo* that had he wanted, he could have denied everything. And one cannot say that we derive it from the fact that it was necessary [for the Torah] to write that a single witness obligates him in an oath — for if one who denies everything were obligated [anyway], what difference would a single witness make, behold, even without it he would be obligated! — for that was necessary in a case where he [the claimant] does not claim anything and does not know, and the witness testifies that he stole, or that his father lent to him. And one can say that from [the verse], "for it is this" (Exodus 22:8), it implies that it is a scriptural decree that specifically one who admits to part of the claim is obligated [in an oath], and not one who denies everything.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:7:1.hebrew: התם ודאי איכא רמאי - לכך קניס ליה גם במה שהוא שלו בודאי. אבל הכא, אימור תרוייהו בהדי הדדי אגבהוה, דליכא רמאי, דכל חד סבור שהוא הגביה קודם:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:7:1.english: There, there is certainly a swindler - For this reason, [Rabbi Yosei] penalizes him even with regard to that which is definitely his. But here, say that both of them lifted it at the same time, so that there is no swindler, as each one believes that he lifted it first.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:8:1.hebrew: אי נמי התם קניס כי היכי דלודי - אבל הכא, אפילו איכא ודאי רמאי, כגון שזה אומר אני מצאתיה היום וזה אומר אני מצאתיה אתמול, מודה דיחלוקו, ולא אמרינן יהא מונח עד שיבא אליהו; דבשביל כך לא יפרוש, דהא אינו מפסיד כלום:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:8:1.english: Alternatively, there [Rabbi Yosei] penalizes so that he will admit - But here, even if there is definitely a swindler—such as where this one says, "I found it today," and that one says, "I found it yesterday"—[Rabbi Yosei] concedes that they divide it, and we do not say, "Let it be placed [in storage] until Elijah comes," for on account of that he will not withdraw [his claim], since he loses nothing.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:9:1.hebrew: אלא מחוורתא כדשנין מעיקרא - נוכל לומר דהדר ביה, ולא סגי בטעמא דמפסיד הרמאי לבד, דלא קניס ר' יוסי אלא היכא דאיכא ודאי רמאי ואית ליה פסידא; אבל היכא דאיכא רמאי וליכא פסידא, לא יקנוס, כדמשמע לישנא דא"כ מה הפסיד הרמאי. מיהו לשון אלא משמע דהדר לגמרי; וכן בסמוך, דפריך: בין לרבנן בין לרבי יוסי, נימא יהא מונח – אף על גב דהתם לית ליה פסידא לרמאי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 3a:9:1.english: Rather, it is clear as we explained initially - We could say that [the Gemara] retracted [only to the extent that] the reason of the swindler suffering a loss alone is not sufficient; for Rabbi Yosei penalizes only where there is definitely a swindler and he incurs a loss, but where there is a swindler and no loss, he would not penalize, as is implied by the wording: "If so, what did the swindler lose?" However, the wording "Rather" [ela] implies that [the Gemara] retracted completely [from the second explanation]; and similarly nearby, where [the Gemara] objects: "Both according to the Rabbis and according to Rabbi Yosei, shall we say let it be left [in escrow]?"—even though there, the swindler incurs no loss.
